Where there is true friendship, both friends will delight in each other.
I cannot explain to you how much joy God has in his people. We will find that out later. But he calls his church his Hephzibah, and he says, “My delight is in her.”
I believe our Lord takes endless delight in a soul that he has made new and shaped to be like himself.
He was glad to see man at the beginning, but later he was sorry he had made man. But the Lord is always glad to see the person he has made new, and he is never sorry that he put him on the earth.
The Lord is pleased with people who fear him.
I am sure that if we are God’s friends, our greatest joy is to come close to God, the God who is our overflowing joy.
Sometimes I have wished I had nothing else to do except spend time with God in prayer, praise, and preaching.
There are a thousand worries and cares that come to me because of smaller matters that grow out of the weaknesses of his church and people. If it were not for them, what a happy life I would have!
I am not really complaining. I only mean that serving God in holiness, while always walking closely with him, is heaven on earth.
But sadly, we have to come down from the mountain where Jesus was transfigured. At the bottom of the hill we meet the suffering boy and the arguing religious teachers.
Our delight is in God.
“Yes, he is my very own God.”
He is my everything.
Everything that comes from him smells sweet, like myrrh and aloes and cassia.
Even his threats sound like music to the people who love him.
There is nothing he does that we will not enjoy.
In the end we even come to love the rod he uses.
The blows of a faithful friend like this are far better than the kisses of our lying enemy.
The cross Jesus puts on us is a light load, because we delight in him.
The God of love has our love, and he has become the light of our joy.
He rejoices over us with singing, and we rejoice before him with joyful music.
But, brothers and sisters, I will not go any further. We must not tell the secrets of love out in the open street.
I see a curtain, a veil that covers the holy of holies.
I don’t dare lift that veil.
Ordinary worshipers cannot go into the most holy place. They cannot even look inside until the Lord anoints their eyes and makes their spirits clean.
O Lord, show yourself to the half-open eyes of your people.

Behind that curtain there are special revelations, secret assurances, and overwhelming joys that I must not speak about. I feel about these things the way Paul felt about what he saw and heard in Paradise. He said it would not be right for anyone to talk about them.
Dear friends, may you know these special joys from your own experience, just as the man did who is called “Friend of God”!
IV. I will be finished once I have said a few words about the last point, which is THE TITLE PUT TO USE in practical ways.
These are the practical uses.
First, this is a great encouragement for God’s people.
Look at what is possible for you.
Not long ago, on a Sunday morning, I tried to say something about what saints may become in the future. After all, the servant who was faithful with his pound was put in charge of ten cities.

It has not yet been shown what we will be. We do not have even the beginning of an idea of what we will be in the next world if we are found faithful to our Master here. Nor do we know the glory that will transform us on the day Christ comes, and during the thousand years of his glorious reign on the earth.
But now I want you to notice the prize of your high calling in this life.
You can become God’s friends. You can be so clearly on his side that people will call you the friends of God.
How few people reach this!
Do you know even one person like that?
Think of all the Christians you know, and tell me how many of them could be called friends of God.
I know one man like that, but I will not say his name.
I am afraid he may not be on earth much longer, because he is very old.
He is a man who has trusted God, walked with God, and been faithful to God. Because of this, God has greatly honored him by letting him carry on a huge and very useful work.
I wish I could grow to be like him, but next to him I feel like a little baby.
He is a rare man.
Why aren’t there more people like him?
Is it because God’s arm is too short?
No. It is because our sins hide him from us.
We could be—and we should be—such men and women that the people who know us at home and at work would see that we are friends of Jesus.

As a preacher, I would like people to say this about me: that I upheld the glory of my Lord, defended the teachings of his cross, and was a friend of the old gospel while others were chasing after new ideas.
In one way or another, we should aim for this heavenly friendship.
See that this is within your reach—and make it real right away.
Next, here is a serious thought for those who want to be God’s friends.
A friend must act like a friend and take tender care of his friend.
One small word from a friend will hurt you much more than a harsh lie from an enemy.
Remember how the Savior said, “It was not an enemy—I could have put up with that. But it was you, a man like me, someone I knew well.”
“The Lord your God is a jealous God.” If he brings any of us so close to him that we become his friends, then his jealousy burns like coals of juniper wood, with a very fierce flame.
My brother, God will save you in spite of a thousand faults. But he will not call you his friend unless you take great care to please him in everything.
Should we back away from this honor because of the responsibility?
No, we are glad to have the responsibility. We long to please God.
Our God is a consuming fire, but we still long to live in him.
Our new nature feels at home in this fire.
Even now we pray that this fire will purify us and burn away all the dross and tin in us.
We would gladly be baptized with fire.
We do not want anything to be spared that should be burned up or that can be burned up.
We accept friendship with God on his terms.
I tremble as I say this.
We are willing to go through anything that will make us one with God.
God’s Spirit is the Spirit of judgment and the Spirit of burning. Do you know what you are asking for when you pray to be filled with him?
I hope you will answer, “Whatever it may be, I want to feel that heavenly influence that can make me God’s friend forever.”
